key_terms: The Hive tool that initializes, upgrades and verifies the Metastore's relational schema version.
Upgrading the Metastore database schema for new binaries. Rolling the binaries back does not reverse the migration.
Checking at startup that the stored schema version matches the binaries, failing clearly instead of upgrading silently.
A consistent dump of the Metastore database with its version information. It cannot restore warehouse files lost from a separate volume.

worked_examples.title: Verify the schema version before startup
worked_examples.code:
cd work/hive
bash run.sh verify-schema
bash run.sh status
worked_examples.interpretation: verify-schema runs schematool -dbType postgres -info in a separate admin container, which prints the Hive distribution version and the metastore schema version stored in the database. The two must agree before the metastore starts. A mismatch does not mean the data is broken; it means the binaries and the stored schema disagree, and starting anyway can let a newer metastore write rows that an older one cannot read back.

worked_examples.title: Take a consistent copy before any upgrade
worked_examples.interpretation: Run against the owned PostgreSQL service, pg_dump takes a single consistent snapshot of the metastore database, and pg_restore --list confirms the archive is readable without restoring it. Test the upgrade against a restored copy in a separate database, never on the live one. If the trial fails, the original remains untouched and the failure output becomes the evidence for planning the real change.

worked_examples.title: Read why the metastore refused to start
worked_examples.interpretation: When versions disagree, the metastore log names the expected and found schema versions and stops. Setting hive.metastore.schema.verification to false would hide that message and let the service run on an incompatible schema, which is the opposite of the safe response. The right fix is either matching binaries or a tested schematool upgrade on a copy, followed by verify-schema again before startup.

evidence: Prepared actual Hive4.2.1/JDK21/PostgreSQL project; live SQL, independent Java Thrift, lifecycle, Iceberg and restore observations remain distinct acceptance gates.
